newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: BMB buys own shares, lifts Bahrain index.
newsitem.headline: BMB buys own shares, lifts Bahrain index.

text.p: Bahrain Middle East Bank's (BMB) ongoing acquisition of up to 10 percent of its own shares is fuelling a sharp rise in Bahrain's stock market, dealers and bankers said on Tuesday.
"BMB wants to acquire 10 percent of its 335 million shares, or 33.5 million shares, from the market," a banker told Reuters. "The bank is now buying its own shares at between 202-204 fils each."
BMB chief executive Albert Kittaneh confirmed that the bank had been buying its shares after receiving permission from Bahrain's authorities to acquire up to 10 percent.
"The bank has bought around 22 million shares," Kittaneh said, adding that he expects further strength in the share price. "We feel that the current BMB share price does not reflect the true value."
BMB's share price soared to 204 fils on Monday from 169 three weeks ago and 140 fils a month earlier. At 0900 GMT on Tuesday the share was quoted at 200 fils.
"The bank will continue to buy its shares if the price is reasonable," Kittaneh said.

Traders said the BMB move, part of a staff share scheme, was the main reason behind a seven percent rise in the overall Bahrain share index in the past three weeks. The index closed on Monday at 1,932.58 points, up from 1,803.54 points on July 28.
Taib Bank said in a statement the BMB move was aimed at using the 10 percent for its employees' stock options and awards scheme.
Dealers said another bank, United Gulf Bank , was also behind some of the recent strength in the market.
On Thursday UGB, 97 percent owned by Kuwait Investment Projects Co , posted net profit of $16.3 million in the first six months of 1997, sharply up from $5.2 million a year earlier.
The bank's share price was at 202 fils at 0900 GMT on Tuesday from 165 fils on July 28 and 148 fils a month earlier.
Traders cautioned that the index could stabilise or ease in the short-term on profit-taking.
"There has to be a price correction. I expect the index to stay put or ease slightly after the recent increase," one said.
But Kittaneh remained bullish: "In my opinion Bahrain's market is undervalued. There is room for further growth."
The Bahrain market is open to Gulf Arab nationals. Some firms are also open to foreign investors.
